text: Why the shift stops at $D_7$ (the pairing lemma). If $x^E\in\gamma_k$, $E=2^s\ge4$, then $E(x-1)\in\Delta^2$, $2E(x-1)\in\Delta^3$, $4E(x-1)\in\Delta^4$ (expand $x^E-1=\sum_m\binom Em(x-1)^m$; for the last step $4\binom E3=\frac{(E-1)(E-2)}3\cdot2E$ and $3\mid(E-1)(E-2)$). Hence $(x-1)(\zeta^{2^{k-2}E}-1)\in\Delta^{2k}$ for $\zeta\in\gamma_k$, $k\le4$: this is the factor $x_1^{16}=x_1^{2E_1}$, $x_2^{128}=x_2^{2E_2}$ in (3.14) ($k=3$). For class 5 ($k=4$) the analogue needs $g_i=\prod_jx_j^{L_{ij}}=\zeta_i^{4E_i}$, while (3.12) has $g_1=\zeta_1^{16}$, $g_2=\zeta_2^{128}$, i.e. $2E_i$. scripts/plateau5_pairing.py enumerates the power-of-2 scalings of $E_i$, of the rows of the exponent matrix and of $L_{ij}$ for which $g_i\in4E_iD$ modulo $\gamma_c$ (121 644 of them); the 80 cheapest, built at class 4, all have $w=1$ in $M$. In this family the two requirements are in tension: $w\ne1$ needs some $L_{ij}<E_iE_j$ (since $[x_j,x_i^{E_i}]$-type factors have order dividing $E_j$), and the quadrupled pairing pushes the $L_{ij}$ up.

text: Lemma 1 [on paper]. Let $Q$ be a finitely generated nilpotent group of class $\le3$ and $n\in\{4,5\}$. Then $D_n(Q)\subseteq\tau(\gamma_3(Q))$ (the torsion of $\gamma_3$), and $\theta:\gamma_3(Q)\to\Delta^3/\Delta^n$, $g\mapsto g-1$, is a homomorphism with kernel $D_n(Q)\cap\gamma_3(Q)$. Hence, if $\tau(\gamma_3(Q))$ is a 2-group, $D_n(Q)=1$ iff $\theta$ is injective on the elements of order 2 of $\tau(\gamma_3(Q))$. Proof. $D_3=\gamma_3$ for every group (classical, see [MP09, ch. 1] †), so $D_n(Q)\subseteq\gamma_3(Q)$. By Jennings the rational dimension subgroups are the isolators: $D_n(Q)\subseteq\sqrt{\gamma_n(Q)}=\tau(Q)$ for $n\ge4$ (Jennings 1955 †; the same fact as Quillen's theorem behind the certificate of §6.4). For $g,h\in\gamma_3$: $gh-1=(g-1)+(h-1)+(g-1)(h-1)$ and $(g-1)(h-1)\in\Delta^6$. A nontrivial subgroup of a finite 2-group contains an element of order 2. $\square$

text: Corollary 2 [on paper]. Let $G$ be a group with $\gamma_5(G)=1$ and $Q=G/\gamma_4(G)$ with $D_5(Q)=1$. Then $D_r(G)\cap\gamma_4(G)=1$ implies $D_r(G)=1$ for every $r\ge5$: the image of $D_r(G)$ in $Q$ lies in $D_r(Q)\subseteq D_5(Q)=1$.

text: Relation to MATH-41 [on paper]. An element of $D_7(G)\setminus\gamma_4(G)$ in a class-4 group gives $1\ne x\in D_5(Q)$ for the class-3 quotient; $x$ has 2-power order, and a finitely generated nilpotent group is residually a finite $p$-group on its $p$-elements (Gruenberg †), so $x$ survives in a finite 2-group of class $\le3$ with $D_5\ne1$: a negative answer to MATH-41 (Kourovka 20.84). So the gap closed here is exactly an instance of MATH-41; the 80 groups $Q$ (three of them, Rf15, Rf16, Rd46f15, finite 2-groups of class 3) all have $D_4=1$, stronger than the $D_5=1$ that MATH-41 asks for. They are instances, not evidence of a general argument.

text: Lemma 3 [on paper]. (i) $\psi:A_4\to\Delta^4/\Delta^n$, $k\mapsto k-1$, is a homomorphism ($(k-1)(k'-1)\in\Delta^8$). (ii) For $K\subseteq A_4$ and $v\in M$: $v\in D_n(M/K)\iff v-1\in\Delta^n+(K-1)A$, and $$(K-1)A+\Delta^n=\Delta^n+\sum_{k}\psi(k)\cdot R,\qquad R=\mathrm{span}\{1\}\cup\{(x_{j_1}-1)\cdots(x_{j_l}-1):1\le l\le n-5\},$$ $k$ over generators of $K$ ($K$ is central, $\psi(k)\Delta^{n-4}\subseteq\Delta^n$, and $\Delta/\Delta^{n-4}$ is spanned by those monomials). Proof. The kernel of $\mathbb Z[M]\to\mathbb Z[M/K]$ is $(K-1)A$, and $\Delta(M/K)^n$ is the image of $\Delta^n$. For $k=\prod k_j^{e_j}$, $\psi(k)\equiv\sum e_j\psi(k_j)$ by (i). $\square$

text: So for a fixed $K$ the question $w\in D_n(M/K)$ is linear: add the rows $\psi(k_j)\cdot r$ to $J_n(M)$. The existence of some $K$ is not: with $\Lambda(k\otimes r)=\psi(k)r$, a $K$ works iff some solution $(k_r)_r\in A_4^{R}$ of $\sum_r\psi(k_r)r\equiv\psi(w)$ (an affine coset of $\ker\Lambda$) has $w\notin\langle k_r\rangle$. "The coordinates of a point of a coset generate a subgroup that misses $w$" is a union over the subgroups $K$ (equivalently over $\varphi\in\widehat{A_4}$ with $\varphi(w)\ne0$), not an intersection: dually, a counterexample is a $\varphi$ that is not of the form $\varphi=\chi\circ\Lambda(\cdot\otimes1)$ for a character $\chi$ of $A/J_n$ with $\chi\circ\Lambda\in\langle\varphi\rangle\otimes\widehat R$ — a rank-one condition on a tensor, which is not linear in $\chi$. This is where a single linear problem stops. What does survive is one-sided:

text: Proposition 4 [on paper]. Let $U_n=J_n+\Lambda(A_4\otimes R_+)$, $R_+$ the monomials of degree $1..n-5$, and $\bar\psi:A_4\to A/U_n$. If $\bar\psi$ is injective, then $D_n(M/K)\cap\gamma_4(M)/K=1$ for every $K\subseteq A_4$. Proof. If $v\in D_n(M/K)\cap A_4$, $v\notin K$, then by Lemma 3 $\psi(v)\in J_n+\psi(K)+\Lambda(K\otimes R_+)\subseteq U_n+\psi(K)$, so $\bar\psi(vk^{-1})=0$ for some $k\in K$, and $v=k\in K$. $\square$
